author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Providence College volleyball opened its home schedule with a straight-sets victory over Manhattan University on Friday night at Alumni Hall. The Friars won 25-14, 25-13 and 25-9 in the opening match of the 21st annual Friar Classic, improving their early-season record to 6-1.

Macy Taylor and Sophia Adkins paced the Providence offense with nine kills apiece. The Friars finished with 40 kills as a team and held Manhattan to a negative attack percentage. Setter Miller McDonald added five service aces and recorded a .957 serving percentage, helping Providence control extended stretches in each set.

Providence used six-point runs in the opening set to create separation, then led the second set from start to finish. The Friars built a 10-4 advantage in the third and stretched the margin to double digits before closing the sweep with back-to-back points. Providence is scheduled to continue the tournament Saturday with matches against Stonehill in the afternoon and Holy Cross in the evening.
dek: The Friars won all three sets by double digits to begin the Friar Classic, improving to 6-1 behind a balanced attack and strong serving.
headline: Providence volleyball sweeps Manhattan in home opener
